step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard depicts a multi-account AWS architecture separating Account A (non-production/isolated) and Account B (production). External actors include a Developer/User represented by a user icon at the top (mapped to UserCompanyDeveloper) and an On-Premises Data Center represented by a building icon at the bottom (mapped to OnPremDC). Within Account A, there are subnets containing NAT Gateway (NAT) in the public subnet and Amazon EKS (EKS) in the private subnet (deduplicated across the two visually identical subnets). Within Account B, AWS WAF (WAF) sits at the entry, followed by an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in the public subnet and Amazon EKS (EKS) in the private subnet. No explicit directional arrows are drawn between the service icons on the whiteboard (only a crossed-out VPC Peering symbol between accounts), so no edges are defined.
